title_en: In re Consolidated Bankruptcy Liquidation of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Tianji Heyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd.
ruling_gist_en: Where affiliated companies have commingling of assets, management, and business operations such that they cannot be separately liquidated, several affiliated companies may be consolidated and liquidated as a single enterprise. The role of the people's court in liquidation is defined as supervision and guidance: supervision is comprehensive, and guidance is macro-level; the court does not intervene in specific liquidation matters to maintain an impartial adjudicative stance. Proceeding from the actual situation where the bankrupt enterprise is effectively absent in bankruptcy-related litigation, and the administrator and the opposing party have asymmetric access to evidence and facts, the trial mode of party autonomy is not simply applied; rather, the application of the inquisitorial trial mode is appropriately and moderately strengthened at the right time.

full_text_en:
Minfa Securities Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. — Consolidated Bankruptcy Liquidation Case

【Ruling Summary】

Where affiliated companies have such commingled assets, management, and operations that they cannot be individually liquidated, several affiliated companies may be consolidated and liquidated as a single enterprise. The court's role in liquidation is to supervise and guide—comprehensive supervision and macro-level guidance—without intervening in specific liquidation matters so as to maintain a neutral adjudicative position. Taking into account the actual circumstances that in bankruptcy derivative litigation, the bankrupt enterprise is effectively absent and the administrator and the opposing party have asymmetrical access to evidence and facts, the court should not simply apply adversary procedure principles but should appropriately and moderately strengthen the application of ex officio procedure principles.

Applicant: Liquidation Group of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Wusi Road, Fuzhou.
Representative: Ma Tengying, Head of the Liquidation Group.

Respondent: Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Wusi Road, Fuzhou.
Legal Representative: Zhang Fuchun, Chairman of the Board.

Respondent: Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Financial Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Ma Zhuang, Chairman of the Board.

Respondent: Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Dongfang Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Zhang Feiguang, Chairman of the Board.

Respondent: Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Yincheng East Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Cao Wei, Chairman of the Board.

Respondent: Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zhongxing Road, Luohu District, Shenzhen.
Legal Representative: Chen Guohua, Chairman of the Board.

On July 5, 2008, the Applicant, the Liquidation Group of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., filed an application with the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter "Fuzhou Intermediate Court") on the grounds that the Respondent, Minfa Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Minfa Securities"), was insolvent and unable to pay its debts as they fell due, requesting that Minfa Securities be declared bankrupt for debt repayment, and that Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Shanghai Yuansheng"), Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Shanghai Quansheng"), Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Beijing Chenda"), and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan") be included in the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings of Minfa Securities for consolidated liquidation.

The Fuzhou Intermediate Court held that the application of the Applicant, the Liquidation Group of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., met the acceptance conditions for bankruptcy cases. With the approval of the Supreme People's Court, and in accordance with Article 10 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 37 of the Regulations on the Disposition of Securities Companies' Risks, the Court ruled on July 18, 2008 as follows:

The case concerning the application of the Liquidation Group of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd. for declaring Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. in consolidated bankruptcy for debt repayment is accepted for filing.

The Fuzhou Intermediate Court found the following facts upon trial:

The Respondent, Minfa Securities, had engaged in serious violations of laws and regulations in its operations. On October 16, 2004, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) appointed China Orient Asset Management Corporation to take over its management under a custodianship arrangement. On July 8, 2005, the CSRC revoked Minfa Securities' securities business license, ordered its closure, and appointed China Orient Asset Management Corporation to establish a liquidation group to conduct administrative liquidation. After Minfa Securities entered bankruptcy liquidation proceedings, an audit and review were conducted. As of July 18, 2008, Minfa Securities was insolvent, with a net book value of RMB -6,999,849,258.09.

Separately, it was found that the Respondents, Shanghai Yuansheng, Shanghai Quansheng, Beijing Chenda, and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan (hereinafter the "four affiliated companies") were important affiliated companies established by Minfa Securities in the names of others to evade supervision. Their registered capital originated from Minfa Securities, and their business premises were the same as those of Minfa Securities' branches. In violation of laws and regulations, Minfa Securities conducted off-balance-sheet entrusted asset management, treasury bond repos, investments, and financing activities through the four affiliated companies. The assets under the names of the four affiliated companies consisted primarily of stocks formed through proprietary securities business conducted pursuant to Minfa Securities' arrangements, while their basic liabilities arose from fund flows with Minfa Securities. The four affiliated companies were severely commingled with Minfa Securities in terms of assets and management, had inadequate corporate governance structures, and served as instruments for Minfa Securities' illegal and irregular operations. The specific circumstances are as follows:

1. False shareholder capital contributions, effectively investments by Minfa Securities. Although Minfa Securities was not the registered shareholder of the four affiliated companies, the audit confirmed that the registered shareholders of these four companies had not actually made capital contributions; their registered capital all came from Minfa Securities.

2. Commingling of organizations and personnel. Shanghai Yuansheng and Shanghai Quansheng operated as "one team, two signboards" and shared office space with Minfa Securities' Shanghai Management Headquarters on the 34th floor of Huaneng Building, No. 958 Lujiazui Ring Road, Pudong Road, Shanghai. The general managers of Shanghai Yuansheng and Shanghai Quansheng upon establishment were both appointed by the general manager of Minfa Securities' Shanghai Management Headquarters. Beijing Chenda and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan were consistently commingled with Minfa Securities' organizations and personnel. Beijing Chenda and Minfa Securities' Beijing Management Headquarters operated under a "one team, two signboards" model and shared office space on the 2nd floor of Haitai Building, No. 229 Beisihuan Middle Road, Haidian District, Beijing. Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan and Minfa Securities' Shenzhen Zhongxing Road Business Department operated under a "one team, two signboards" model and shared office space at the Foreign Trade Center Building on Zhongxing Road, Shenzhen.

3. Commingling of operations. The basic cooperation model between Minfa Securities and the four affiliated companies was as follows: Minfa Securities' relevant functional departments, in the names of the four affiliated companies, accepted matched funds or raised external financing through tripartite supervision; they collected external financing funds from other units under Minfa Securities used by the relevant functional departments; and they issued fund transfer notices and conducted securities transactions to the four affiliated companies. The four affiliated companies were primarily responsible for matters such as: opening fund accounts and shareholder accounts, effecting fund transfers, designating and canceling designations of shareholder accounts, and carrying out proprietary liquidation for Minfa Securities.

4. Commingling of assets. Since the four companies primarily cooperated with Minfa Securities in securities business pursuant to its instructions, their main assets consisted of proprietary securities. The types of stocks held were relatively concentrated and similar to those heavily held by Minfa Securities (Shuanghe Pharmaceutical, Liaoning Chengda, and Inner Mongolia Mengdian). Specifically, as of July 18, 2008, the market value of proprietary securities of Shanghai Yuansheng accounted for 92.79% of its total assets, of which the market value of Shuanghe Pharmaceutical accounted for 99.62% of the total market value of proprietary securities; for Shanghai Quansheng, the market value of proprietary securities accounted for 28.22% of total assets, of which the market value of Shuanghe Pharmaceutical accounted for 98.05% of the total market value of proprietary securities; for Beijing Chenda, the market value of proprietary securities accounted for 98.20% of total assets, of which the market value of Liaoning Chengda accounted for 83.65% and Inner Mongolia Mengdian accounted for 14.12% of the total market value of proprietary securities; for Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan, the market value of proprietary securities accounted for 96.08% of total assets, of which the market value of Liaoning Chengda accounted for 99.71% of the total market value of proprietary securities.

5. Commingling of liabilities. As of July 18, 2008, Shanghai Yuansheng's liabilities to Minfa Securities accounted for 97.92% of its total liabilities; all of Shanghai Quansheng's liabilities were liabilities to Minfa Securities; Beijing Chenda's liabilities to Minfa Securities accounted for 98.89% of its total liabilities; and all of Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan's liabilities were liabilities to Minfa Securities.

Further investigation revealed that, upon audit and review, as of July 18, 2008, all four affiliated companies were insolvent on the books. Specifically, the net assets of Shanghai Yuansheng were RMB -1,268,700,065.02; the net assets of Shanghai Quansheng were RMB -1,298,328,984.99; the net assets of Beijing Chenda were RMB -270,467,489.25; and the net assets of Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan were RMB -94,889,084.94.

The Fuzhou Intermediate Court held:

Although the four affiliated companies were formally independent legal persons, based on the above facts, they were in fact instruments used by Minfa Securities to conduct illegal operations, lacked independent legal personality, and lacked the legal basis for separate bankruptcy liquidation. The reasons are twofold: First, the independence of a legal person lies primarily in the independence of its will—the ability to independently form and express its intent and engage in civil activities. However, the personnel of Beijing Chenda and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan were commingled with those of Minfa Securities' Beijing Management Headquarters and Shenzhen Zhongxing Road Business Department, respectively; and although Shanghai Yuansheng and Shanghai Quansheng had independent staff, actual control of the companies was in the hands of Minfa Securities' Shanghai Management Headquarters. Therefore, the external conduct of the four affiliated companies was subject to the control of Minfa Securities, and they lacked the ability to independently express intent. Second, the key to the independence of a legal person lies in the independence of its property—a legal person can bear civil liability with its independently controlled property. The entire business activity of the four affiliated companies was to cooperate with Minfa Securities in conducting illegal securities operations; they had no other independent business activities and generated no business income. The sole source of assets for the four affiliated companies was shareholder capital contributions, which in substance all came from Minfa Securities, and the assets formed from such contributions were also actually controlled and used by Minfa Securities. Therefore, the four affiliated companies had no independently controlled property and lacked the material basis for independently bearing civil liability.

In summary, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court held that Minfa Securities, by engaging in illegal and irregular operations, disrupted the order of the securities market, caused huge losses, and damaged the legitimate rights and interests of investors. Its assets were clearly insufficient to pay its debts as they fell due, and it should be declared bankrupt and liquidated in accordance with law to repay debts. The four affiliated companies, established with capital contributions from Minfa Securities and severely commingled with Minfa Securities in management and assets, lacked independent corporate legal personality and were tools used by Minfa Securities to evade supervision and conduct illegal off-balance-sheet operations. They should be declared bankrupt together with Minfa Securities in consolidated liquidation. In accordance with Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, the Court ruled on October 28, 2008 as follows:

1. Minfa Securities Co., Ltd. is declared bankrupt;
2. Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Tianjiheyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. are declared bankrupt in consolidation with Minfa Securities Co., Ltd.

The specific circumstances of the trial and liquidation of the consolidated bankruptcy case of Minfa Securities and the four affiliated companies are as follows:

I. The Court's Supervision and Guidance of the Liquidation Work

In accordance with the spirit of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the court's role in liquidation is to supervise and guide. In the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, given the complexity of the liquidation work, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court established the basic principles of comprehensive supervision, macro-level guidance, and active judicial role. While refraining from intervening in specific liquidation matters to maintain a neutral adjudicative position, the Court actively explored and innovated mechanisms to strengthen supervision and guidance, providing sufficient institutional safeguards for the Minfa Securities liquidation work. As a result, the ordinary creditor recovery rate increased from an initial expectation of 15%-20% to 63%, ensuring the smooth progress and conclusion of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy proceedings.

(A) Strengthening the Court's Trial Capacity and Leading the Bankruptcy Proceedings in Accordance with Law

1. Innovating the trial management mechanism

To address the complex and intricate realities of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court explored and innovated in the trial management mechanism:

(1) It specifically established a leadership group for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case. The president personally served as the group leader, with the heads of relevant departments and responsible court leaders participating. The leadership group was responsible for addressing the policy, directional, and coordination aspects of the case.

(2) It adopted a trial model where a dedicated collegiate bench centrally handled the relevant trial work. After filing the case, the Court selected experienced personnel from various departments to form a dedicated collegiate bench for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, consisting of up to 12 members. The responsible court leader served as the presiding judge, and the head of the collegiate bench served as the principal adjudicator. The bench was dedicated to hearing cases related to the bankruptcy, compulsory liquidation, and derivative litigation of Minfa Securities and its affiliated companies. The dedicated collegiate bench was listed separately from the Court's other trial divisions and managed independently as a department of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court.

(3) It strengthened financial and human resources support. This included: The Fuzhou Intermediate Court secured a special budget of RMB 4 million for the dedicated collegiate bench to cover trial expenses; when a large amount of concentrated property preservation or evidence collection was needed within a short period, trial personnel were temporarily reassigned from various departments of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court to assist; and 8 grassroots courts also participated in the relevant trial work.

2. Determining the overall approach to liquidation work

(1) Clarifying the role of the trial function and ensuring that supervision was proper without overstepping. On the one hand, the Court insisted on playing a leading role in the bankruptcy proceedings, grasping the overall situation of the liquidation work at the macro level, timely proposing working principles and guiding opinions, guiding the administrator in establishing rules and regulations, and supervising the liquidation work in accordance with law. On the other hand, the Court fully respected the rules of judicial power, maintained neutrality between the administrator and other parties, and insisted that the specific liquidation work be carried out by the administrator. The Court's guidance was limited to overall and principled matters, and judges did not intervene in the handling of specific liquidation matters.

(2) In light of the actual circumstances of Minfa Securities, the Court established a working approach focusing on auditing off-balance-sheet assets and uncovering concealed assets as the centerpiece of the trial and liquidation work, and required the administrator to strengthen the organic linkage between legal and financial aspects during the liquidation process.

3. Actively advancing the bankruptcy proceedings in accordance with law

(1) Some of Minfa Securities' assets were off-balance-sheet or registered under the names of third parties. To prevent nominal holders from maliciously reselling assets or other courts from erroneously enforcing them, at the initial stage of the case, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court deployed over 50 judicial officers to conduct comprehensive preservation of suspected assets of Minfa Securities across 42 cities and 123 units nationwide, preserving assets totaling RMB 5.4 billion, thereby gaining overall control over the bankruptcy estate.

(2) The Minfa Securities liquidation work required coordination and cooperation from multiple departments. The Fuzhou Intermediate Court relied on the superior courts, local party committees, and government authorities to coordinate related issues arising in the bankruptcy liquidation, effectively promoting the resolution of such issues. In particular, during the distribution of securities assets in kind, given the complexity of distributing stocks held in 1,200 natural person accounts to over 170 creditors, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court communicated extensively with the CSRC, China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited, and the Shanghai Stock Exchange; all distribution work was completed within just one week.

(B) Supporting and Supervising the Administrator's Work in Accordance with Law

1. Implementing a project management system for liquidation matters

Given the large volume, complexity, and difficulty of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation work, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court guided the administrator in establishing a project management system for liquidation matters. This involved breaking down and detailing the liquidation work, registering each matter as a separate project, ensuring one project per item, and designating specific handling and responsible personnel. At the same time, the Court strengthened progress management over individual liquidation matters and improved the completion and approval system for each liquidation project. Before the conclusion of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation, the administrator completed a total of 3,700 significant liquidation projects. The project management system not only facilitated the Fuzhou Intermediate Court's supervision of the administrator but also promoted scientific internal management for the administrator, ensuring orderly and efficient progress of the liquidation work.

2. Guiding the administrator in implementing digitization of archives

The original Minfa Securities had chaotic archive management, with incomplete and non-standard files, fragmented historical records, and documents scattered across various locations, making file retrieval and use difficult. To standardize archive management and facilitate inquiries, under the guidance of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court, the administrator engaged an intermediary agency to digitize the relevant case archives and adopted a unified document and archive management system to enable online retrieval and use. In the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, approximately 320,000 pages of significant liquidation materials were organized and digitized, achieving full sharing of various specialized archival information resources.

3. Supporting and assisting the administrator's investigative work

Investigations were a necessary prerequisite for liquidation work such as auditing and recovering Minfa Securities' assets, especially off-balance-sheet assets, reviewing and confirming claims, and representing Minfa Securities in litigation and arbitration. Given the incomplete nature of Minfa Securities' archives, investigations were particularly important. In this case, for matters that the administrator could not investigate on its own, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court issued investigation orders to the administrator to conduct the investigation; if the administrator could not obtain results even with an investigation order, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court would conduct the investigation itself upon application. In this case, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court assisted in over 1,500 investigative matters cumulatively.

(C) Protecting Creditors' Right to Information and Right to Supervision in Accordance with Law

To fully protect creditors' right to information and right to supervision, under the guidance of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court, the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case adopted the following measures:

1. Safeguarding creditors' right to information and right to supervision through the creditors' committee

On December 6, 2008, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court convened the first creditors' meeting of Minfa Securities. At this meeting, in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, members of the Minfa Securities creditors' committee were elected, including China Securities Investor Protection Fund Corporation, New China Life Insurance Company, Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd., China Export & Credit Insurance Corporation, and one employee representative of Minfa Securities, totaling 9 members forming the Minfa Securities creditors' committee. In daily work, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court required the administrator to diligently implement relevant systems, ensuring that material matters such as significant asset disposals and litigation, distribution of bankruptcy assets, and review of rights were reported to the creditors' committee or submitted for its deliberation. In addition, the Fuzhou Intermediate Court required the administrator to proactively and voluntarily accept supervision by the creditors' committee, carefully consider and implement the opinions and suggestions of committee members regarding the administrator's work. In the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case, the creditors' committee basically met once every quarter.

2. Holding regional creditor symposiums

Given the large number of creditors and the short duration of creditors' meetings, to ensure creditors' right to information and right to supervision, under the leadership of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court, the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case held 20 regional creditor symposiums based on the geographical distribution of creditors, enabling creditors to engage in in-depth communication and exchange with the judges of the Fuzhou Intermediate Court and the administrator on issues of concern.

3. Establishing a website for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation

In addition to the above measures, the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case also made full use of modern information technology by establishing a website for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation. Major matters of the case were promptly published on the website, and responses were provided to questions of common concern to creditors, providing convenient access for creditors to understand the progress of the case.

II. Review and Confirmation of Claims and Right of Recovery

As of December 26, 2012, the administrator of Minfa Securities had accepted claims from 203 creditors, with the total declared amount reaching RMB 14,848,070,381.04. After review, 196 creditor claims were confirmed, totaling RMB 11,394,160,462.26. Thirty-five applications for the right of repossession were received, involving property valued at RMB 1,219,561,002.76; 14 applications were denied, 21 were granted in whole or in part, and the confirmed repossession target amount was RMB 521,354,040.02.

Most of the claims declared by creditors of Minfa Securities arose from entrusted investment management arrangements. Given the complexity of defining the legal relationship in entrusted investment management, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court, through the Fujian High People's Court, submitted a *Request for Instructions Report on the Legal Nature of Entrusted Investment Management Contracts with Guaranteed Minimum Return Clauses and the Calculation Standards for Interest Losses in the Bankruptcy Claims Review of Minfa Securities Company* to the Supreme People's Court. The Supreme People's Court replied as follows:

1. Regarding the legal validity of entrusted investment management contracts with guaranteed minimum return clauses, a distinction should be made based on whether the entrusted assets are held in independently operated securities accounts and fund accounts opened in the name of the principal. If the entrusted assets are in independently operated securities accounts and fund accounts opened in the name of the principal, the legal validity of the entrusted investment management contract shall be affirmed. Because the entrusted assets operated in independent securities accounts and fund accounts can be distinguished from the securities company's own assets and those of other clients, the assets in the entrusted investment management accounts shall belong to the principal, and the invalidity of the guaranteed minimum return clause does not affect the principal's right to reclaim such assets. Where the principal directly delivers the entrusted assets to the securities company for management, rather than opening separate fund accounts and securities accounts in the principal's name with the securities company for independent operation, then, depending on the specific provisions of the guaranteed minimum return clause in the entrusted investment management contract, the principal's claim shall be determined either as an illegal inter-enterprise loan or as arising from an invalid entrusted investment management contract. The principal shall handle such claims by declaring an ordinary claim and cannot exercise the right of repossession.

2. If the securities company misappropriates the entrusted securities operated within an independent securities account, and the relationship is clear and the property has not been commingled, the administrator may recover such assets, and the relevant right holder may exercise a substitutional right of repossession. If the misappropriated entrusted securities are commingled with the securities of other clients but remain separate from the securities company's own securities, the entrusted securities and the other clients' securities are not part of the securities company's property subject to claims of other creditors; the principal and other clients may exercise the right of repossession in proportion to their securities. If the misappropriated entrusted securities are commingled with the securities company's own securities, the principal cannot exercise the right of repossession. If the securities company misappropriates funds operated within the principal's independent fund account, causing the funds to be lost or commingled, the principal cannot exercise the right of repossession and must handle the matter by declaring an ordinary claim.

3. If the entrusted assets operated within independent securities accounts and fund accounts generate profits, and the contract includes a profit-sharing ratio, the profits shall be divided according to that ratio. The portion belonging to the securities company shall be distributed as part of the bankruptcy estate.

4. When determining the principal's right of repossession over entrusted assets operated within independent securities accounts and fund accounts, any high interest, fixed returns, or commissions already paid by the securities company to the principal shall be deducted from the property to be repossessed.

5. For entrusted assets operated within independent securities accounts and fund accounts that cannot be recovered due to the securities company's illegal misappropriation, as well as for cases where the principal directly delivered entrusted assets to the securities company for management without opening separate fund accounts and securities accounts in the principal's name, the principal shall exercise an ordinary claim in the bankruptcy proceedings and calculate interest losses based on the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period. If the principal exercises the right of repossession over entrusted assets operated within independent, closed securities accounts and fund accounts, no calculation of interest losses is involved.

Based on the above reply from the Supreme People's Court, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court and the administrator of Minfa Securities reviewed and confirmed a total of 155 claims related to entrusted investment management, with the confirmed amount totaling RMB 8,001,697,633.16.

III. Trial of Bankruptcy-Derivative Lawsuits

(A) Timely and Appropriate Strengthening of the Ex Officio Trial Model

The Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court accepted a total of 1,555 derivative lawsuits arising from the Minfa Securities bankruptcy. These involved various types, including equity confirmation, shareholder derivative actions, entrusted investment management, real estate, securities, and futures. Different types of lawsuits all exhibited characteristics such as the de facto absence of one party and asymmetry in information and evidence. Specifically:

1. One party—the bankrupt enterprise—was de facto absent. Although creditors ultimately bore the consequences of the relevant cases, most could not personally participate in the litigation. Moreover, due to factors such as the dispersion of creditors of the bankrupt enterprise, lack of professional knowledge, and information asymmetry, creditors often found it difficult to effectively supervise the relevant cases.

2. Asymmetry in information and evidence among the parties. When taking over the bankrupt enterprise, administrators frequently faced numerous handover issues, such as loss or damage of corporate records and the disappearance of knowledgeable employees. Compared with the opposing parties who were fully informed of the case facts, administrators often held a weak position in obtaining and gathering evidence. Particularly in the case of Minfa Securities, which had long suffered from chaotic management, extensive off-book illegal and irregular operations, inaccurate financial records, and the unwillingness of many knowledgeable insiders to cooperate with investigations or testify in court, and the deliberate destruction or concealment of relevant business records, the administrator alone often could not adequately collect evidence, making it difficult to effectively protect the interests of creditors.

3. Complexity involving other litigation participants. Since the outcome of derivative lawsuits would ultimately be borne by the creditors of the bankrupt enterprise and often had no interest connection to the enterprise's former employees, the interest alignment of former employees could easily shift. Due to relationships built over long-term business dealings with the opposing party, or due to the lure of personal gain, former employees of the bankrupt enterprise—including many senior managers and business personnel of the former Minfa Securities—might collude maliciously with the opposing party to conceal evidence, provide false testimony, and harm the interests of the bankruptcy creditors.

Given the above circumstances, to achieve substantive justice in derivative lawsuits while also considering litigation efficiency, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court did not simply apply the adversarial trial model. Instead, it timely and appropriately strengthened the ex officio trial model. On the one hand, it increased supervision over the litigation conduct of the administrator and other parties to prevent situations such as fabricating bankruptcy claims, false admissions, and malicious mediation. On the other hand, it strengthened relief for the bankrupt enterprise's side in areas such as assisting with investigations and evidence collection and extending the time period for submitting evidence. Specifically, the following work was carried out:

1. At the level of case facts and evidence, based on factors such as the intensity of adversarial nature of the case and the relationships among litigation participants, the court timely strengthened the review and supervision of the conduct of various participants, paying attention to preventing various types of litigation fraud.

2. At the level of the right to dispose of claims in relevant cases, the court strengthened the review of the right of disposition of the parties, especially the administrator. For mediation applications by the parties, the court paid full attention to the legality of mediation and emphasized mediation based on clarified facts to avoid malicious mediation.

3. In supervising the liquidation work, the court strengthened supervision over the administrator's litigation work. This was reflected in two aspects: first, ensuring that the administrator acted diligently and dutifully in litigation work, preventing unjust judgments due to the administrator's errors or moral hazards; second, actively urging the administrator to initiate lawsuits in situations where the administrator might be reluctant to do so.

4. In assisting with investigations and evidence collection, the court strengthened relief for the inherently disadvantaged bankrupt enterprise side.

5. In allocating the burden of proof in relevant cases, the court reasonably allocated the burden of proof based on the specific circumstances of the case. When the administrator truly did not know the facts due to specific reasons such as handover obstacles in the bankrupt enterprise, the burden of proof was shifted to the opposing party who was aware of the relevant facts.

6. With respect to the time period for submitting evidence in relevant cases, the court carefully applied the rule of evidence preclusion. In the absence of malice or gross negligence on the part of the bankrupt enterprise, the court avoided, as much as possible, using the time limit for submitting evidence to penalize the bankrupt enterprise, thereby avoiding harm to the interests of the vast number of innocent creditors.

(B) Special Collegial Panel for Centralized Trial of Derivative Lawsuits

Due to the large number of derivative lawsuits arising from the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, the seamless coordination between the bankruptcy case and the derivative lawsuits was crucial to the effectiveness of both types of cases. To achieve overall coordination of the bankruptcy case and comprehensive court supervision of the liquidation work, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court adopted a trial management mechanism whereby the special collegial panel hearing the bankruptcy case also tried the derivative lawsuits. To this end, based on the professional fields involved in the cases, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court specially selected 12 judicial officers with extensive trial experience in bankruptcy, corporate, securities, real estate, and labor dispute fields to form the special collegial panel for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case. The presiding judge was a leader of the court in charge; the head of the collegial panel served as the presiding judge for the bankruptcy case. This panel was dedicated to hearing the bankruptcy cases, compulsory corporate liquidation cases, and derivative lawsuits related to Minfa Securities and its affiliated companies. The above judicial personnel formed two collegial panels: one primarily heard bankruptcy cases while also handling lawsuit cases; the other primarily heard lawsuit cases.

(C) Strengthening Coordination between Lawsuit Cases and Overall Liquidation Work

In bankruptcy proceedings, litigation matters significantly constrained the progress of non-litigation matters. For example, rulings on disputed bankruptcy claims, especially those involving large amounts, affected the distribution ratio and timing of distribution of the bankruptcy estate; rulings on ownership of disputed subject matter affected the realization of the bankruptcy estate. Therefore, when trying the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court placed great emphasis on coordinating non-litigation and litigation matters. By properly trying related lawsuit cases, it facilitated litigation fairness and substantive justice, effectively supported the overall work progress of the bankruptcy case, better played the court's leading role in bankruptcy proceedings, and significantly improved the efficiency of bankruptcy liquidation.

The above measures and work achieved significant results in trying the derivative lawsuits of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case. In the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court concluded 1,535 derivative lawsuits, achieving a case closure rate of 99% and an enforcement rate exceeding 95%, effectively ensuring the smooth progress of the overall liquidation work.

IV. Distribution of Bankruptcy Estate

Given the complexity of Minfa Securities' bankruptcy estate and bankruptcy claims, to ensure timely satisfaction of creditors, the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case adopted a model of multiple distributions. Specifically: The first bankruptcy estate distribution plan was executed on January 10, 2010, with ordinary debt repayment rate of 37.91%; the second plan was executed three times (July 2010, December 2010, and July 2011), with ordinary debt repayment rates of 12.468%, 1.95%, and 1.22%, respectively, totaling 15.638%; the third plan was executed on December 29, 2011, with an ordinary debt repayment rate of 9.46%. After the execution of the three plans, the total ordinary debt repayment rate in the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case reached 63.008%.

Among these, for securities assets heavily held by Minfa Securities, such as Liaoning Chengda and Shuanghe Pharmaceutical, following review and voting by the creditors' meeting, in-kind distribution was adopted. The stock price was calculated based on the respective average closing prices of Shuanghe Pharmaceutical and Liaoning Chengda stocks over the 60 trading days following the date the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the distribution plan.

V. Termination of Bankruptcy Proceedings

The Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court and the administrator considered that, according to the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the basic condition for terminating bankruptcy proceedings is the completion of distribution of undisputed bankruptcy estate. According to the project management system for the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case, as of April 2012, the administrator had initiated 3,739 projects and completed 3,700, with a completion rate of 98.96%. The conditions for terminating the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation case were substantially satisfied. Additionally, pursuant to Article 122 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, pending or unresolved lawsuit and arbitration cases did not affect the termination of bankruptcy proceedings.

Based on the above facts, to smoothly terminate the Minfa Securities bankruptcy proceedings, in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and considering the actual circumstances of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy case, the administrator completed the following work:

1. On January 5, 2012, the administrator published the *Public Announcement on the Final Distribution of the Bankruptcy Estate of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd.* in the "China Securities Journal," "People's Court Daily," and "Fujian Daily," announcing that the third distribution of the Minfa Securities bankruptcy estate would be the final distribution.

2. The administrator sent a *Letter Soliciting Opinions on Matters Related to the Termination of the Minfa Securities Bankruptcy Proceedings* to all creditors. Under the leadership of the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court, the administrator also held multiple regional creditor symposiums nationwide to broadly solicit creditors' opinions on matters such as arrangements for terminating the Minfa Securities bankruptcy proceedings. Statistics showed that over 95.45% of creditors supported and agreed with the arrangement to terminate the bankruptcy proceedings after the execution of the third distribution plan.

3. The third creditors' meeting reviewed and approved the *Report on Residual Matters and Work Arrangements After Termination of Bankruptcy Proceedings of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd.* submitted by the administrator. Its main contents included: retaining the administrator institution to handle residual work; electing representatives of six creditors, including Jilin State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd. and China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., to supervise the administrator's work after the termination of proceedings.

After the creditors' meeting, no creditor raised objections to the termination of bankruptcy proceedings.

Based on the above work, the administrator applied to the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court for a ruling to terminate the Minfa Securities bankruptcy liquidation proceedings.

Upon review, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court held that: The distribution of undisputed bankruptcy estate in this case had been completed. Disputed bankruptcy estate had entered other legal proceedings for resolution. The statutory conditions for terminating the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings had been satisfied. Additionally, the applicant had made appropriate arrangements for unfinished liquidation work, and thus the bankruptcy proceedings could be terminated. Given that there remained residual liquidation work such as pending lawsuits and enforcement matters, the administrator should be retained to continue performing liquidation duties after the termination of bankruptcy proceedings. After deliberation by the Adjudication Committee, and pursuant to Article 120, Paragraphs 2 and 3, and Article 122 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, on December 13, 2012, the court ruled as follows:

The consolidated bankruptcy proceedings of Minfa Securities Co., Ltd., Shanghai Yuansheng Investment Management Co., Ltd., Shanghai Quansheng Investment Development Co., Ltd., Beijing Chenda Technology Investment Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Tianjihuiyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. are hereby terminated.
